welcome.subject: Welcome to Veinote, {{name}}
welcome.body_1: Welcome to Veinote. You've just opened a space built for one thing: finishing songs you're proud of.
welcome.body_2: Your canvas is ready whenever you are: lyrics, melody notes, and ideas all in one flow.

collab_invite.subject: {{inviter}} invited you to write a song on Veinote
collab_invite.preheader: {{inviter}} started “{{project}}” and wants you in it. Start free.
collab_invite.body_1: {{inviter}} is writing “{{project}}” on Veinote and wants you in the room. Veinote is where songwriters draft lyrics, record takes and finish songs together — in the same project, at the same time.
collab_invite.body_2: Start free. Your first {{days}} days are on us, no card charged, and everything below opens the moment you join {{inviter}}:
features: Write together in the same project — up to 5 people, live
The canvas: lyrics, takes and files in one flow
Demo studio: record straight from your laptop
Rhyme lexicon and dictionary, in English, Norwegian and Swedish
Guitar tuner and tap tempo, right where you're writing
Material that gets you writing, from fundamentals to the full bank of tips
The community: meet other songwriters and share what you finish
You own 100% of everything you write

collab_invite.ignore: Not your kind of thing? You can ignore this email and nothing happens.

beta_welcome.subject: Welcome to the Veinote beta, {{name}}
beta_welcome.preheader: Your sign-in details are below, plus four things to try first.
beta_welcome.body_1: You're one of the first songwriters inside Veinote. We're starting with a small group, so we can hear what works and what doesn't. Your account is ready, so there's nothing to sign up for.
beta_welcome.body_2: Sign in with the details below. The password is temporary. Once you're in, use “Forgot password?” on the sign-in page to pick your own.
beta_welcome.credentials_note: Please keep this email to yourself. Anyone with these details can open your account.
beta_welcome.tasks_title: What we'd love you to do
beta_welcome.task_1_body: Take one idea from a blank canvas to a song you'd play someone. Lyrics, takes and notes all live in the same flow. That's the part we most want tested.
beta_welcome.task_2_title: Learn a new tip and use it
beta_welcome.task_2_body: Open Learn, pick a tip you haven't tried, and use it on the song you're writing. Then tell us if it made a difference.
beta_welcome.task_3_body: Run at least one session in Practice. Tell us straight if it was worth your time. If it wasn't, that's just as useful for us to know.
beta_welcome.task_4_body: Post your finished song in Community, and leave feedback on someone else's. The room only works when people are in it.
beta_welcome.feedback: If anything breaks, confuses or annoys you, use “Share feedback” in the sidebar or just reply to this email. Small annoyances count too. Those are the ones nobody reports and nobody fixes.
beta_welcome.signoff: Thanks for building this with us,

practice.mapping_pending_desc: It may be too short or too quiet for the analyser. You can still listen — accuracy improves with every update.
practice.goal_master_song_structure: Rebuild real songs section by section until you hear how verse, chorus and bridge hold each other up.
practice.goal_composing_verses: Turn one theme into five singable lines, using your own nouns and verbs as the raw material.
practice.goal_melody_harmony: Find melodies that sit naturally over your chords, and chords that lift the melody you already have.
practice.goal_advanced_structures: Break the standard form on purpose — pre-choruses, false endings and sections that shift under the listener.
practice.goal_free_hand_session: No steps and no scoring. Write against the clock and see what turns up.
practice.goal_finding_hooks: Write the one line the whole song hangs on, then cut it until nothing is left to remove.
practice.goal_rhyme_without_cliche: Chase the rhymes nobody expects — near rhymes, internal ones, and the ones that land off the beat.
practice.goal_rhythm_and_phrasing: Say the same line five ways until you find the one that sits in the pocket.
practice.goal_telling_a_story: Move a listener from the first line to the last without ever explaining yourself.
practice.goal_chord_progressions: Build progressions you can hum over, and learn why the tired ones still work.
practice.goal_imagery_and_detail: Trade adjectives for things you can see, hear and touch.
practice.goal_titles_that_stick: Collect titles first and write towards them, instead of hunting for one at the end.
practice.goal_bridges_that_turn: Write the eight bars that change what the chorus means when it comes back.
practice.goal_writing_from_a_feeling: Start with a mood and no words, and let the first honest line decide the song.
practice.goal_co_writing_session: Hand the pen back and forth, and practise finishing someone else's line.
practice.select_theme_desc: Select the emotional anchor for your verses
practice.link_desc: Connect nouns with verbs 1 by 1 (order doesn't matter)

studio_guide.title: Studio Guide
studio_guide.headphone_warning: For the best timing, use wired headphones. Bluetooth may cause recording delay.
studio_guide.env_tip_1: Find a quiet, carpeted room (avoid echo)
studio_guide.env_tip_2: Close windows & shut down background fans/AC
studio_guide.tech_tip_1: Position mic 10-15 cm from your mouth
studio_guide.tech_tip_2: Set level so peaks don't clip (avoid red zone)
studio_guide.equip_tip_2: Choose a high-quality USB/XLR condenser mic

studio_banner.warning_text: For the best timing, use wired headphones. Bluetooth may cause recording delay.
studio_banner.before_you_record_sub: You do not need professional equipment to use Demo Studio. Your device's built-in microphone is enough to get started.
studio_banner.tip_headphones_desc: Headphones prevent the previously recorded tracks and metronome from being recorded again through your microphone.
studio_banner.tip_wired_desc: Bluetooth headphones can create noticeable delay while recording. For better timing, use headphones connected with a cable.
studio_banner.tip_mic_desc: Before recording, make sure Demo Studio is using the microphone you want to record with.
studio_banner.tip_quiet_desc: Background noise and room echo will become part of your recording. A quiet room with curtains, furniture, or other soft surfaces usually sounds better.
studio_banner.tip_pos_desc: Stay close enough to get a clear sound, but not so close that the recording becomes distorted.
studio_banner.tip_apps_desc: Closing other audio, video, or browser applications can improve performance and reduce interruptions.
studio_banner.recommended_setup_sub: For a simple and reliable recording setup, we recommend:
studio_banner.higher_quality_note: For higher-quality recordings, you can use an audio interface with a microphone or instrument connected to it.
studio_banner.about_bluetooth_desc: Bluetooth headphones are useful for listening, but they are not recommended while recording. Bluetooth introduces latency, which means you may hear the sound slightly later than you play or sing.

items.question: Do I need to know music theory to write a song?
items.answer: No. Many famous songwriters write by ear and emotion. Veinote helps turn your musical ideas into finished songs, with no music degree needed.

items.question: What comes first: the lyrics or the melody?
items.answer: There is no right way! Some start with a melody, others start with lyrics. Veinote works with both, helping you easily combine words and music.

items.question: My lyrics feel "cheesy." How do I fix them?
items.answer: Lyrics feel cheesiest when you describe feelings too directly. Veinote helps you show rather than tell, suggesting details and patterns to make your songs feel real.

items.question: How long should it take to write a song?
items.answer: A song can take 15 minutes or several months. Our tools are built to help you get started right away and finish your songs in hours, not weeks.

type_notes.lyricist: The words come first, and they have to be the right ones. You'd rather write one line that lands than ten that fill space.
type_notes.melodist: You hear it before you can explain it. The tune arrives whole and the rest of the song has to catch up.
type_notes.producer: You think in arrangement: what enters, what drops out, what the song sounds like finished.
type_notes.storyteller: Every song belongs to someone, and you can't start until you know who. Character before chorus.
type_notes.explorer: You write to find out what you think. The song is the search, not the report.
type_notes.default: You already write. What you need is somewhere that keeps up with you.

struggles.unfinished: You start songs and don't finish them. The parts end up in notes, voice memos and files you never open again.
struggles.weak_melodies: You have the words. The melody is the part that never gets good, and you have nowhere to sing it out loud.
struggles.no_structure: You have good pieces, but they don't add up to a song.
struggles.too_similar: New songs keep coming out sounding like the last one.
struggles.overthink: You rewrite the first line so many times you never reach the second.
struggles.default: Something keeps getting between you and a finished song.

fixes.unfinished: Veinote keeps one song in one place. Words, voice notes and files sit on the same canvas, so you pick it up where you left it instead of starting again.
fixes.weak_melodies: Sing the idea straight into the demo studio, then try ten more in a few minutes. Every take is kept, so you can go back to the one that worked.
fixes.no_structure: The canvas lays the song out in sections. You see what you have, what's missing, and where a part belongs.
fixes.too_similar: The rhyme and word tools hand you options you wouldn't have reached for, and you can write with someone else when one head isn't enough.
fixes.overthink: Park a line, keep writing, come back to it later. Nothing you try is lost, so a bad idea costs you nothing.
fixes.default: Veinote keeps the whole song in one place and helps you get it finished.

dreams.finish_songs: In three months you have finished songs you'd play for someone without saying sorry first.
dreams.unique_sound: In three months someone hears eight bars and knows it's yours.
dreams.move_people: In three months you have the song that makes a room go quiet.
dreams.release_music: In three months you have a song ready to release, and somewhere to send it.
dreams.creative_fearless: In three months you try things without worrying about wasting the day.
dreams.write_for_loved_ones: In three months you have played someone the song you wrote for them.
dreams.feel_better: In three months writing is where you go to feel better, not one more thing you owe yourself.
dreams.meet_songwriters: In three months you have writers you send half-finished songs to, and who send you theirs.
dreams.earn_money: In three months you know what your songs are worth, and who pays for them.
dreams.default: In three months you have songs that are finished, not just started.

meta.title: Veinote: The home of human songwriting
meta.description: No AI-generated songs. You create them. You own them.

about.intro: No AI-generated songs. You create them. You own them. Veinote combines creative tools, expert guidance, and a supportive community to help songwriters actually finish what they start.
about.story_p1: Most songwriters never finish their songs. Not from a lack of talent or ideas, but because the process from first lyric to finished recording has no clear path, and it's easy to lose momentum somewhere in the middle.
about.story_p2: Veinote was founded in 2026 in Stockholm by a small team of songwriters and builders, including co-founder Peter Nordberg, a platinum-selling, top 2% songwriter worldwide with over 30 years of experience and 250+ released songs. His lessons, exercises, and creative frameworks guide songwriters through every stage of the platform.
about.story_p3: We believe songwriting is a human craft. As AI-generated music becomes more common, we're building the opposite: tools that help you write, finish, and own songs that are genuinely yours.

pillars.learn: Bite-sized lessons and exercises that build real songwriting craft, one idea at a time.
pillars.create: A canvas built for lyrics, melodies, voice notes, and ideas to come together in one flow.
pillars.practice: Guided sessions that turn theory into muscle memory, so writing songs gets easier every time.
pillars.connect: A community of songwriters sharing work, feedback, and encouragement along the way.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.body: Veinote ("we", "us", "our") operates veinote.com and the Veinote platform. This policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and the choices you have. By using Veinote, you agree to the practices described here.

info_we_collect.title: Information we collect
info_we_collect.body: We collect information you provide directly, such as your name, email address, and password when you create an account. We also store the content you create on Veinote (lyrics, voice recordings, images, documents, and project data) so it can be saved and shown back to you. We automatically collect basic usage data, such as which pages and features you use, to help us understand and improve the product.

how_we_use.title: How we use your information
how_we_use.body: We use your information to provide and maintain the platform, save and sync your songs and progress, respond to support requests and feedback, send account-related and product emails, and improve Veinote's features and reliability. We do not sell your personal information.

your_content.title: Your content
your_content.body: The lyrics, recordings, and other creative content you make in Veinote belong to you. We store it so you can access and edit it across sessions and devices, and we do not use your creative content to train AI models.

cookies_analytics.title: Cookies & analytics
cookies_analytics.body: We use essential cookies to keep you signed in and to remember basic preferences. We also use analytics tools, including Microsoft Clarity, to understand how the site is used so we can improve it. Analytics data is used in aggregate and is not sold to third parties.

third_party.title: Third-party services
third_party.body: Veinote relies on trusted third-party services to operate, including Firebase (authentication, database, and file storage) and email delivery providers for transactional messages. These providers process data on our behalf and are bound by their own privacy and security obligations.

data_security.title: Data security
data_security.body: We use industry-standard measures, including encrypted connections and access controls, to protect your information. No method of storage or transmission is completely secure, but we work to keep your data safe and to respond quickly if something goes wrong.

data_retention.title: Data retention & deletion
data_retention.body: We keep your account and content for as long as your account is active. You can request deletion of your account and associated data at any time by contacting us. See below.

your_rights.title: Your rights
your_rights.body: Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, export, or delete your personal information. To exercise any of these rights, contact us and we'll respond as quickly as we can.

childrens_privacy.title: Children's privacy
childrens_privacy.body: Veinote is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: We may update this policy from time to time. If we make material changes, we'll let you know by posting the updated policy here with a new effective date.

contact.title: Contact us
contact.body: Questions about this policy or your data? Reach us any time at support@veinote.com.
